clue.text: Quiet couple returning after Greek signs of expansion

indicators.note: after puts the turned pair behind the abbreviation for Greek
returning tells us to read the quiet-plus-couple pair backwards

parts.note: SH is the call for quiet
a couple is two

explanation.surface: Two hushed people walk back behind a Greek, watching for hints that something is spreading.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' reads the quiet-and-couple pair backwards; 'after' puts that behind the Greek abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Growths are the visible marks of something getting bigger, so they are signs of expansion.

clue.text: Marooned pirate protecting old lady's shooter

indicators.note: protecting means wrapped around, so the pirate's name surrounds the mother

parts.note: Ben Gunn is the marooned pirate in Treasure Island
ma is an informal word for mother, one's old lady

explanation.surface: A castaway buccaneer guards a mother's gun.
explanation.definitionFit: A gunman is a person carrying a gun, a shooter.

clue.text: Tannoy's adjusted to limit decibels, ready for use

indicators.note: to limit means to enclose, so the rearranged letters surround the decibel abbreviation
adjusted means altered, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: dB is the abbreviation for decibels

explanation.surface: A public address system is tuned to cap its loudness, ready to go.
explanation.walkthrough: A Tannoy is a British public address loudspeaker brand. 'adjusted' gives ONSTANY, and 'to limit' has it enclose the decibel abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Equipment on stand-by is kept ready to be used at short notice.

clue.text: Source of timber cut on ledge over supporting frame

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: a tree is where timber comes from

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the ledge word reads backwards

parts.note: a sill is a ledge, as under a window

explanation.surface: Wood sawn on a shelf above some framework, like a carpenter's workshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Source of' looks like a first-letter signal, but the whole phrase means TREE, which 'cut' trims; 'over' turns SILL to LLIS, and 'on' merely links.
explanation.definitionFit: A trellis is a lattice framework that supports climbing plants.

clue.text: Legal visit interrupted by teacher

indicators.note: interrupted by means the teacher word breaks into the middle of the visit word

parts.note: a stay is a visit
a tutor is a teacher

explanation.surface: A lawful holiday cut short by a schoolmaster.
explanation.definitionFit: Statutory means required or permitted by statute, so it is legal.

clue.text: Tom possibly eating fool, a cold dessert

indicators.note: eating means the cat word swallows the fool word

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, the 'possibly' marking it as one example
an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A tomcat devours an idiot, then a chilled pudding is mentioned, like a strange menu.
explanation.definitionFit: Cassata is an Italian ice-cream dessert layered with fruit and nuts, served frozen.

clue.text: Thick piece of meat from part of camel below its head

indicators.note: below places the hump under the head letter in this down answer
its head is the opening letter of the camel just named

parts.note: the part of the camel meant is its hump

explanation.surface: A butcher's cut taken from a camel just beneath its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'part of camel' is HUMP; 'camel' also supplies its head letter C on top.
explanation.definitionFit: A chump is a thick cut of lamb or mutton from the loin end.

clue.text: Senior pilot who makes short hops

definitions.meaning: the captain of an aircraft or ship

explanation.surface: A senior airline captain who only flies brief routes.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is a captain in charge, and literally someone who skips along.

clue.text: Dismay person from Arctic area heading north

indicators.note: heading north in a down answer means reading upwards

parts.note: a Lapp is one of the Sami people of Arctic Scandinavia

explanation.surface: Someone from the far north travels upward and is horrified.
explanation.definitionFit: To appal is to fill with horror, which is to dismay.

clue.text: Close friend of a lieutenant before leave

parts.note: ere is an old word for before
to go is to leave

explanation.surface: A junior officer's best mate, met before he departs.
explanation.definitionFit: Alter ego, Latin for other self, is used for a trusted intimate friend.

clue.text: Freak of nature's a bloodsucker

indicators.note: a freak is something twisted out of its normal form, so the following letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A monstrous creature of nature turns out to be a vampire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Freak of nature' looks like one noun phrase, but 'Freak' is the anagram signal working on OF NATURE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Nosferatu is the vampire of the 1922 silent film, and a vampire is a bloodsucker.

clue.text: Power to stop one fanatic's contribution

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: to stop means to plug a gap, so the power letter sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: a nut is a fanatic or enthusiast
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Someone tries to use power to halt a single zealot's offering.
explanation.definitionFit: Input is what someone puts into a shared effort, their contribution.

clue.text: What do you say we draw over an embarrassment — benefit?

indicators.note: asking what you say points to how the words are pronounced

parts.note: the idiom is to draw a veil over something embarrassing, so what we draw is a veil

explanation.surface: A conversational question about tactfully hiding an awkward moment, ending by asking if there is any gain.
explanation.definitionFit: Avail as a noun means use or advantage, as in 'to no avail', which is a benefit.

clue.text: Mix up Ron and Paul, having few friends

indicators.note: mix tells us to stir the following letters into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone confuses two men named Ron and Paul, which hardly helps their social standing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mix up' reads as a phrasal verb, but only 'Mix' is the signal; UP is part of the letters rearranged, with Ron and Paul.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unpopular is disliked by most people, and so has few friends.

clue.text: Worrying cancellation of musical performances?

definitions.meaning: read as dis- plus concerting, the undoing of concerts; the question mark flags the invented sense

explanation.surface: A troubling case of gigs being called off.
explanation.definitionFit: Something disconcerting unsettles and troubles you, which is what worrying means here.

clue.text: Aware of insignificant worker, maybe a worker covering bad practice up

indicators.note: covering means wrapping around, so the two worker words enclose the turned sin

parts.note: a cog is a small, unimportant part of an organisation
an ant is the classic worker insect

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the sin letters read from the bottom

parts.note: a sin is a wrongdoing

explanation.surface: A lowly employee, probably a drone, conceals misconduct.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' marks ANT as one example of a worker; the reversed sin goes between the two workers.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognisant means having knowledge of something, so it is a synonym for aware.

clue.text: Rude about five unable to pay debts

indicators.note: about means going round, so the rude word surrounds the numeral

parts.note: insolent means rude
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Someone is cheeky about a fiver because they are broke.
explanation.definitionFit: An insolvent person or firm lacks the means to pay what it owes.

clue.text: Look to step on garden tool, always wanting revenge at last it's best served cold

indicators.note: each piece in turn lacks the final letter of the word revenge

parts.note: to gaze is to look
a pace is a step
a hoe is a garden tool

explanation.surface: Stepping on a rake and getting whacked makes someone vow vengeance, a dish best served cold.
explanation.walkthrough: The last letter of 'revenge' is E; GAZE, PACE and HOE each lose an E.
explanation.definitionFit: Gazpacho is a Spanish tomato soup eaten chilled, so it is best served cold, borrowing the proverb about revenge.

clue.text: Impossible to know time lost by arbitrary visitors at funeral?

parts.note: any, as in any one at random, means arbitrary

indicators.note: lost by says the time letter drops out of the phrase that follows

parts.note: mourners at a funeral are guests of the deceased, the body

explanation.surface: A puzzled account of random mourners at a funeral, whose time has gone.
explanation.walkthrough: ANY BODY'S GUESTS loses its last T.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that is anybody's guess cannot be known for sure; the idiom means it is uncertain.

clue.text: Work exercises covered in talk

indicators.note: covered in means the exercises sit inside the talk word

parts.note: to orate is to talk, especially pompously
PE, physical education, is school exercises

explanation.surface: Workouts get discussed at length.
explanation.definitionFit: To operate is to function or run, which is a sense of work, as a machine works.

clue.text: Tangle up globe with green coating

indicators.note: up in a down answer means the whole assembly reads from the bottom
coating means wrapping round, so the green word encloses the globe

parts.note: lime is a shade of green
an orb is a globe

explanation.surface: A ball wrapped in green fabric gets knotted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' belongs with 'Tangle' in the surface but turns LIORBME into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To embroil is to entangle someone in a conflict or difficulty.

clue.text: Little woman after gaining weight and marrying twice?

indicators.note: after places the Alcott sister behind the size word

parts.note: someone who has gained weight is big
Amy March is one of the sisters in Alcott's novel Little Women

explanation.surface: A small woman puts on pounds and weds two husbands.
explanation.definitionFit: Bigamy is the crime of marrying one person while still married to another; the question mark admits the loose wording.

clue.text: Topping one found after look round double edge of pizza?

definitions.text: Topping one found after look round double edge of pizza?

indicators.note: found after places the topping and numeral letters behind the enclosed look word
round means surrounding, so the look word encloses the doubled edge letter

parts.note: to peer is to look closely

indicators.note: double means the edge letter is used twice
the edge of a word is its outer letter, here the first

parts.note: on is on top of, a topping
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The whole clue describes a pizza slice whose edge you look round to find a topping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Topping' reads as the definition but gives ON; the whole clue defines the answer, a classic all-in-one.
explanation.definitionFit: Pepperoni is a spicy salami sliced as a favourite pizza topping, which the whole clue describes.

clue.text: Don't be sad with chapter excised and turned to pulp

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the rest reads backwards
excised means cut out, so the chapter letters go

parts.note: cheer up is what you tell someone who is sad

explanation.surface: A sad book loses a chapter and is pulped.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excised' leaves EERUP, and 'turned' gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A purée is food mashed or blended to a smooth pulp.

clue.text: Start transposing notes

indicators.note: transposing means swapping positions, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A musician begins moving music into another key.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transposing notes' sounds like music, but it rearranges the letters of NOTES.
explanation.definitionFit: An onset is the beginning of something, as at the onset of winter.

clue.text: Spicy dish? There's tons in Indonesian province

indicators.note: in places the tons letter within the province name

parts.note: Bali is an island province of Indonesia

explanation.surface: A question about whether there is a lot of hot food on an Indonesian island.
explanation.definitionFit: A balti is a spiced curry cooked and served in a metal bowl, an example of a spicy dish, hence the question mark.

clue.text: A brief soreness in neck when rotated roughly

indicators.note: rotated means turned round, so the letters are read in reverse
brief means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: a crick is a painful stiffness in the neck

explanation.surface: A short-lived stiff neck when you turn your head, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brief' trims CRICK to CRIC; 'when rotated' turns A CRIC around.
explanation.definitionFit: Circa is Latin for about, used before approximate dates, so it means roughly.

clue.text: Thus each period produces ongoing drama

parts.note: so means thus
a pop is informal for each, as in five pounds a pop
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Every stretch of time in turn yields a never-ending story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each' is not A or PER here but the informal A POP.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap opera is a serial broadcast drama that runs on indefinitely.

clue.text: Covered path, with outsiders wanting pig out?

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so each word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A sheltered walkway, with strangers turned away, where a pig might be let out.
explanation.definitionFit: To pig out is slang for gorging yourself, which is to overeat; the question mark flags the slangy phrase.

clue.text: Author narrated tale, omitting every fourth part

indicators.note: every fourth letter of the phrase is dropped

parts.note: a narrated tale is a told story

explanation.surface: A writer recounted a story but skipped some sections.
explanation.walkthrough: In TOLD STORY the fourth and eighth letters are D and R.
explanation.definitionFit: Leo Tolstoy, Russian novelist of War and Peace, is a famous author.
